title: Service account governance playbook and provisioning API
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Create an operational playbook plus a small provisioning API to standardize service account creation, ownership assignment, least-privilege templates, and audit telemetry. This ticket codifies guardrails for service account lifecycle (create, transfer, rotate, revoke), ties templates into RBAC v2 roles, and adds audit events to the central logging pipeline. Goal: reduce ad-hoc SA creation and improve auditability for Dedicated and Private deployments.
acceptance_criteria: A stable JSON schema for service-account templates documented in Confluence and validated with unit tests
An internal provisioning API (POST /internal/service-accounts) that enforces template-based least-privilege roles and emits AuditLog.create events to the audit pipeline
Ownership model implemented: every SA must have an owner (user/team) and an automated grace flow for unowned SAs after 30 days
Automated rotation TTL and recommended KMS/HSM integration patterns documented
End-to-end e2e tests that create/transfer/delete SAs and assert audit records are emitted and RBAC checks enforced
Security review completed and signed off by security@redwood with remediation items tracked
tasks: Define canonical service-account template schema (fields: name, purpose, recommended-roles, ttl-days, rotation-policy, owner-team, allowed-scopes)
Design RBAC v2 role mappings for common templates (read-only, ingest-worker, model-servant, infra-admin) and publish mappings to permissions registry
Implement provisioning API with validation and owner-assignment hooks (service: sa-provisioner)
Emit structured audit logs for create/transfer/rotate/revoke events (schema version sa-audit-v1)
Add UI helper in Console for requesting new SA using templates (frontend ticket separate), include prefilled recommended roles
Implement a nightly job to detect unowned SAs and notify owners and infra-ops for manual remediation
Write integration tests for audit pipeline ingestion and retention checks
Create migration utility to convert legacy ad-hoc SAs into template-backed SAs with suggested role diffs

rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): Enable template-only creation for platform and infra teams in staging
Phase 2: Open template creation to all internal teams, require owner assignment
Phase 3: UI integration in Console and email/webhook notifications for unowned SAs
Phase 4: Migration run to suggest template binding for legacy SAs and opt-in conversion
migration_plan: Inventory ad-hoc SAs using query https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/sa-inventory
Run diff against recommended template roles and generate review tickets for owners
Batch-convert low-risk SAs during weekend maintenance window; notify stakeholders
Retire legacy SA APIs after 90 days post-migration with final audit report
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Overly-strict templates block valid platform use cases. Mitigation: allow template extensibility and a documented 'escalate-to-admin' flow.
Risk: Missing owner leading to orphaned credentials. Mitigation: nightly detection + auto-notify + enforcement after grace period.
Risk: Audit log schema change breaking downstream retention. Mitigation: schema versioning (sa-audit-v1) and consumer compatibility tests.
testing_plan: Unit tests for template validator and RBAC mapper
Integration tests that assert audit events land in Kafka and are parsed by audit-consumer
E2E test that simulates owner transfer and ensures old owner loses access immediately
Load test to verify provisioning API can handle expected burst during oncall rotations
notes: This ticket intentionally avoids automating secret rotation; ops playbook will include runbooks and recommended tooling (Vault/KMS) for rotation automation later
Consider adding SSO/SAML group sync for owner-team membership as follow-up (linked to RBAC v2 group sync epic)
Follow-up UX ticket for Console inclusion: PM to create after API contract stabilized
